mission.display_title: Evaluate probabilities and quantiles for placed families
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to turn Beta's family placement into probability and quantile evaluation — so you can compute or obtain P and quantile answers for the univariate families you already recognise, without pretending Poisson-process or generation LOs are finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to evaluate probabilities and quantiles for named univariate families using calculation or software as appropriate — and to refuse treating family recognition alone as evaluation skill.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from 'I can place the family' to 'I can evaluate a probability or quantile for that family with an honest method warrant.'
mission.learning_objective: Evaluate probabilities and quantiles associated with the basic univariate distributions already placed (by calculation or using statistical software as appropriate).
mission.concept_focus: Named family → probability or quantile question → method (tables/software/calculation) → refuse recognition-as-evaluation theatre.
mission.prior_bridge: Campaign Beta ended after continuous family placement (2.1.2) and Revision. Today continues topic 2.1 at LO 2.1.3 — evaluation — not a new chapter leap.
mission.why_now: 2.1.3 is the named Continuity Front after CS1-002. Closing it prevents the day-9 cliff while keeping Poisson process and generation as later days.
mission.expected_benefit: Study Progress for probability/quantile evaluation — not Topic Complete for 2.1.4–2.1.6.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Gamma Day 1 because CE-001 / EP-001 Continuity Front names 2.1.3 as the handoff from Beta.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: probability vs quantile
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For a named continuous family (e.g. Normal or exponential): (1) state one probability evaluation question in words; (2) state one quantile evaluation question in words; (3) name one acceptable method class (calculation / tables / software).
knowledge_checks.body: Distinguish P-questions from quantile questions; name a method class.
hints: Probability: find P(X ≤ a) or similar.
Quantile: find x such that P(X ≤ x) = p.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Evaluation skill starts by discriminating the question type and method class.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Example: Probability — find P(X ≤ 2) for X ~ Exp(λ). Quantile — find x such that P(X ≤ x) = 0.95. Method — software CDF/quantile functions or calculation/tables as the CMP allows.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Restating the family name without posing an evaluation question.
success_criteria: Distinct probability and quantile prompts stated.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: evaluate and refuse recognition theatre
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A portfolio loss is modelled as approximately Normal. You need the 95th percentile loss. (1) What evaluation type is this? (2) What do you compute or call? (3) Refuse in one sentence: 'I know it is Normal, so I am finished without evaluating.'
knowledge_checks.body: Identify quantile task; name Normal quantile/software step; refuse recognition-as-done.
hints: Need mean/sd (or standardised) then quantile function / tables.
Refuse: naming the family is not the numerical answer.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Quantile evaluation for Normal is not completed by family placement alone.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Quantile / percentile evaluation. (2) Use the Normal quantile (tables or software) at 0.95 with the fitted mean and sd. (3) Refuse: knowing the family names the model; it does not produce the percentile without evaluation.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Stopping at 'use Normal' without stating the quantile step.
